mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a quarter indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% in a quarter signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of periods with a sustained increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a robust labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k & UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 2% in a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods with a sustained increase in GDPC1.
